_about: Boeing vs Airbus war-game adjudication parameters. Money in $B (constant 2026 dollars), PV'd to years.pv_base at each player's WACC. Every value is tagged in wargame/README.md as CALIBRATED (taken from the combined_dash.py landmarks) or PLACEHOLDER (edit freely).

ramp_options._about: The briefing's 'Launch fps with 7-year / 10-year ramp-up': how fast production ramps after entry into service. A slower ramp captures share more slowly but needs less capacity capex. PLACEHOLDER.

cfm_leap_plus.label: CFM LEAP derivative (no new engine)
cfm_leap_plus._about: What a new airframe flies when CFM/GE plays and has not committed a new narrowbody engine. PLACEHOLDER until calibrated.

cfm_open_fan.label: CFM RISE open fan
cfm_open_fan._about: available_eis: the open fan cannot enter service before 2045; an airframe that would be ready earlier waits for it, paying extension capex for each waiting year. Launch in 2037 to enter service in 2045 without waiting.

strain._about: Overlap-aware strain: a player developing an NB program and a WB program at the same time pays full_overlap_b x clamp(overlap_years / norm_years, 0, 1), spread over the overlap years and alpha-loaded like capex.

quiet_turn.title: Quiet turn
quiet_turn.narrative: No major external shock this period.

nb_demand_shock.title: Narrowbody demand shock
nb_demand_shock.narrative: A traffic downturn and airline deferrals cut narrowbody deliveries by 10% for three years.

wb_demand_boom.title: Widebody demand boom
wb_demand_boom.narrative: Long-haul traffic recovers faster than forecast; widebody demand rises 15% for the rest of the game.

engine_maturity_slip.title: Next-generation engine maturity slips
engine_maturity_slip.narrative: Engine OEMs report durability issues; next-generation engine technology is ready two years later than planned.

supply_chain_crunch.title: Supply-chain crunch
supply_chain_crunch.narrative: Castings, forgings and labour shortages make running concurrent programs 50% more expensive from now on.

certification_scrutiny.title: FAA certification scrutiny on Boeing
certification_scrutiny.narrative: Regulators tighten oversight of Boeing: programs in development slip one year and new Boeing launches need one extra development year.

fuel_price_spike.title: Fuel price spike
fuel_price_spike.narrative: Jet fuel prices spike and stay high; airlines pay 1.5 pp more margin for new-generation efficiency.

boeing_quality_escape.title: Boeing quality escape
boeing_quality_escape.narrative: A production quality escape grounds deliveries: Boeing loses 2 pp of narrowbody share for three years.

trade_dispute.title: Transatlantic trade dispute
trade_dispute.narrative: Tariffs on imported aircraft cut both manufacturers' margins by 1 pp for five years.

rr_durability_crisis.title: Rolls-Royce widebody durability crisis
rr_durability_crisis.narrative: Hot-section durability problems ground part of the Trent fleet. Rolls-Royce pays for spare engines, shop visits and airline compensation: its incumbent widebody engines earn 40% less lifecycle value for four years.

ultrafan_test_setback.title: UltraFan test setback
ultrafan_test_setback.narrative: Ground tests of the UltraFan gearbox and fan system find problems. Every Rolls-Royce engine program in development slips two years; airframes waiting for it wait longer.

gtf_durability_crisis.title: GTF durability crisis
gtf_durability_crisis.narrative: A manufacturing flaw forces early removals and inspections across the GTF fleet. Pratt & Whitney pays for spare engines, shop visits and airline compensation: its incumbent narrowbody engines earn 50% less lifecycle value for four years.

gtf_next_test_setback.title: Next-generation GTF test setback
gtf_next_test_setback.narrative: Durability testing of Pratt & Whitney's next engine finds hot-section problems. Every Pratt & Whitney engine program in development slips two years; airframes waiting for it wait longer.

suppliers._about: Optional supplier players, the engine makers. Each plays only when a run is created with --suppliers <id>[,<id>] (sets active). Its payoff is the lifecycle value of the large civil engines it delivers versus the status quo, in $B PV to years.pv_base at its WACC. Parameters are tagged in wargame/README.md.

ramp._about: A new engine earns start_frac of its lifecycle value per engine at EIS, rising linearly to 100% after `years` (early durability and learning costs).

A new engine earns start_frac of its lifecycle value per engine at EIS, rising linearly to 100% after `years`. A negative start_frac means it destroys value at first (OE losses and early durability costs, as on the GTF).

objectives._about: Assigned mission objectives per player, from the Boeing Product Development narrowbody briefing (Aerospace Game-Theory Briefing, Boeing Strategy, slide 4; Boeing proprietary). The referee scores attainment alongside delta PV; objectives never change the payoff. Each player sees only its own entry. Metrics are measured on the engine's projection at key years.
